note: From OpenStreetMap's main API (14 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs and the export's railway=rail ways), the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/poynton.jpg) and the photos (docs/reference/photos/poynton: building-1.jpg, platform-train-1.jpg and platform-1-sign-1.jpg Graham Hogg 2019, platform-1.jpg and booking-hall-1.jpg Chris Morgan 2019, carpark-1.jpg and approach-1.jpg John Topping 2013, platform-overview-1.jpg Nigel Thompson 2011), at real scale: two side platforms of about 103 m on the Macclesfield line, 1.68 m outside its two tracks. The halt's platform (towards Manchester) is the export's platform 2, on the south-west side, -v, by the car park and the booking office; positive v is north-east. OpenStreetMap's tracks and platforms lie about 3.5 m further towards -v than the network's tracks do here, so everything from the export is moved 3.5 m towards +v to stand on them. Chester Road (A5149) crosses on a skewed bridge just beyond the platforms' south end, so the extension is at the north end (the game's; the real platforms take about four cars). Trains stop 20 m north of the station's point, so a two-car unit stands on the platforms as they are and a six-car one once they're extended. The covered footbridge with its stairs, the 1887 brick booking office behind the halt's platform and the brick building with its canopy on the far platform from the export and the photos (platform-train-1.jpg, platform-overview-1.jpg, whose caption has it looking north, but the export and the view from above put the road bridge at the south end); the roofs drawn hipped, the heights and the bridge's build not surveyed. The car park and the covered cycle stands from the export. The rail replacement buses use the Railway Station stop on Chester Road (the export). Lamps, boards and shelters placed by eye; the lifts, barriers, kiosk and coffee cart are the game's.
